analyst_view.overall: This is a relegation scrap. Estoril are bottom and still without a league win. Vasco Matos left by mutual agreement in late October, and on 3 November interim Sérgio Raimundo was made head coach for the rest of the season, despite no wins in his first three games (1-3 v Moreirense, 0-4 at Porto). Marítimo (8 pts) have gone eight league games without a win under Mitchell van der Gaag and lost 2-0 at home to Santa Clara last Sunday.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, which looks high for two struggling sides. Estoril have scored once in two league games under Raimundo, and top scorer Yanis Begraoui (20 goals last season) is only a hope after missing four games. Marítimo have scored just 3 in their last six, and both sides have plenty to lose in a six-pointer.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.1 corners. Estoril at home should push for a first win, but nothing specific in the news moves the corner count.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. A bottom-of-the-table meeting with a new coach under pressure on one bench and an eight-game winless run on the other usually brings more fouls and bookings. José Bessa referees.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots. Raimundo has said the ball 'doesn't want to go in', which suggests Estoril are getting shots away and not finishing them, so we do not move the shot count.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target. Without Begraoui, and with Fabrício Garcia and Isra Salazar also out, Estoril's finishing has been poor, and Marítimo have barely threatened in recent weeks.
